description:
It's 8:14 on a Tuesday morning in March. You're on the downtown train in New York, half asleep, with forty people around you. You blink. And they're gone. More than eight billion people just disappeared. Everyone except you.

This is the full story, all three years in one film: your first year alone in Manhattan with a dog named Bagel, a fire on a rooftop that finally gets an answer, a sixty-four-year-old cargo pilot named Ruth, a flight across the top of the Atlantic, nine strangers at the top of the world, and the answer to who was flying that jet.

Which day would have broken you first? Tell me in the comments.

Become a member and support the channel: https://www.youtube.com/@HardyHumans/join

WHAT'S REAL AND WHAT ISN'T
Everyone vanishing is fiction, and so are Hardy, Bagel, Ruth, the nine in Svalbard and Signe's flight. The science around them is real. New York's water really flows by gravity from reservoirs more than 100 miles north, and that pressure only reaches about six floors. The subway's pumps really move about 13 million gallons of water on a normal day. In 2003 a few overloaded lines in Ohio really blacked out about 50 million people in minutes. Alexander Selkirk really lived alone on an island for more than four years, and lit a fire when he saw ships. JFK's fuel farm really holds about 36 million gallons. The Svalbard Global Seed Vault really keeps the backup seeds of the world's crops inside an Arctic mountain. And a fighter that landed on the Greenland ice sheet in July 1942 was really dug out fifty years later from under 268 feet of ice, and flew again.

This is a story, not a guide. Never walk on subway tracks, never run a generator indoors, never drive into flood water, and never fly into icing your plane isn't certified for.
